title: Opt-out automatic referral triggers for early specialist palliative care in outpatient oncology: protocol and results of a pragmatic stepped-wedge trial
abstract: Background: referral to specialist palliative care is late at a regional cancer centre. Design: pragmatic stepped-wedge trial in eight clinics switching in randomised pairs from usual referral to opt-out automatic referral triggers over five 3-month periods. Primary outcome: days alive and out of hospital in the 90 days after trigger eligibility, from routine records. Results and conclusions will be written after the trial.
introduction: Palliative care delivered alongside oncology treatment is associated with less aggressive end-of-life care in recalled studies, but referral depends on individual oncologists and is often late. Automatic triggers could make referral systematic; two recorded searches found no evaluation of outpatient opt-out triggers.
methods: Eligible patients are identified by the same electronic rules in both conditions. Referrals in trigger periods are sent unless the oncologist opts out within 5 working days. A linear mixed model with period and clinic effects estimates the difference in days alive and out of hospital.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present clinic flow by period, trigger volume, opt-outs and declines, the primary estimate with its confidence interval, the process, secondary and balancing outcomes, and results by distance, language and deprivation.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the estimate against time trends and capacity, compare it with the literature once it has been retrieved and checked, and state what the centre will do with the triggers.
limitations: Eight clusters; possible contamination before switching; routine data without symptom or quality-of-life measures; evidence base not yet retrieved.
conclusion: To be written after the trial; it will be limited to the outcomes measured and will not claim effects on quality of life that were not measured.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for stepped-wedge cluster randomised trials; TIDieR
summary: CONSORT-structured draft with results left empty until the trial ends.
